subject: Where to put a local data directory?

messages.author: d061848075edfc55
messages.subject: Where to put a local data directory?
parts:
I'm attempted to deploy my first app on shinyapps.io.  In the app, the user selects a file from a drop down menu, and the data file is plotted.   I am confused where to put the directory with the data so that the app can access it; I keep getting the "ERROR: Cannot change working directory" message.

My directory is like so:  server.R, ui.R and data directory (called MyData) are located in /MyShinyApp.  When I deploy the app using deployApp() (which works fine), a directory called shinyapps is created in /MyShinyApp, with a subdirectory /MyUsername which contains a MyShinyApp.dcf file.  I am using the follow relative path to tell the app where my data is: setwd("./MyData").  Any suggestions on where to move the MyData directory so that my app can access it?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: d061848075edfc55
messages.subject: Re: Where to put a local data directory?
parts:
After searching the showLogs() for my app, I was able to figure out what was going on.  My data directory was in the right location, and it was being uploaded to the server, but for some reason using relative file paths to change the working directory was not work for me.  

Using the absolute file path setwd("/srv/shiny-server/MyApp/MyData") worked, but relative filepaths setwd("./MyData") did not work.  Its a little strange because when I run deployApp(), the function warnings me that I'm using absolute paths, and I should use relative file paths instead.  Not sure if this is a bug or not.

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Where to put a local data directory?
parts:
Ken,

Thanks for sending the files.

I did a quick check, but didn't have time to go through it thoroughly. 

When I run your application locally, after changing the absolute paths to relative paths, I see the error on changing directory. So this is not a problem only on shinyapps. Do you not see any errors running locally?
This points to the fact that your current directory changes during the application run. I added a little output of getwd() to the first page, and verified that your current directory in fact changes. 
So it seems that the function(s) that set the directory to a directory within your application gets called again. The first time the call is successful, but any subsequent time, this will cause error as your current directory has already changed. So setwd with absolute path will always work, but with relative path will only work once, unless you set it back to the top level. I didn't get deep into your code, and can't tell where/how to set it back. You would know better. Or alternatively, do not use setwd(), but access the data and function files using a relative path.

Hope this helps!

Best,
Fereshteh
